weaknesses: The paper does not state its main message plainly. The fixed-overlap result shows that latent stationary overlap gives no rate improvement for any fixed C>1: the rate is still T^{-beta}, the Hu–Wager rate without the condition. The only gain is in the shrinking layer q_C ≲ T^{-1/2}. This is a sharp contrast with MehrabiWager2025, where strong distributional overlap on an observed Markov state gives the parametric rate. The introduction instead says the analysis 'characterizes how that cost changes', and the related work calls the result 'an occupancy-overlap analogue'. Fix: add an introduction paragraph and a discussion paragraph saying that bounding the latent stationary density ratio, unlike the fully observed case, keeps the partial-history exponent for every fixed C. Say directly whether the Hu–Wager lower-bound instance violates latent stationary overlap. Novelty depends on that answer, so give a precise theorem locator for their lower bound.

The 'radius-adaptive' estimator is tuned by an oracle. κ_T^rad(C) requires knowing q_C, t_0 and ζ, and the fixed depth k_T already attains T^{-beta} for every C. The only practical gain from the adaptive depth is when the analyst knows the overlap radius shrinks at a known rate. Fix: rename it (for example 'radius-calibrated depth'). Say explicitly that attaining the frontier as stated requires knowing (t_0, ζ, C). Add a Limitations sentence on data-driven depth selection and whether adaptation to an unknown q_C costs a log factor.

The assumptions are restated but never weighed. Latent stationary overlap bounds d_e/d_b on unobserved states, so it cannot be checked from the observed trajectory. Uniform total-variation contraction over all initial laws, for both policies, is a Doeblin-type condition that fails for many clinical dynamics. Policies are restricted to be binary, memoryless and known, with a stationary start. The lower bound needs a latent alphabet that grows like log T, so the rates may not describe a model with fixed |H|. The local path C_T = 1+δ_T with δ_T → 0 has no applied motivation. Fix: add a subsection after the model class. For each condition, give an interpretation, say how an analyst would argue for it, state which results use it, and say what is known when it fails (especially fixed |H| and non-stationary starts).

The insulin section overstates what the example shows. The reward depends only on observed glucose, and the bias diagnostic is the difference between behavior-stationary and target-stationary reward averages. It would be nonzero with diet observed, so nothing links it to latency. The bound C=720 gives q_C≈0.9986, so the example sits in the fixed-overlap regime and says nothing about the frontier. Yet the text claims 'latent dietary occupancy is the source of stationary weighting bias' and 'Consequently, the adaptive observable-history estimator ... is the relevant estimator'. Fix: either compute the diagnostic with diet moved into X and compare, or drop the latent-source claims. Report q_C and the implied κ_T, and describe the example only as a check that the model class can hold in a stylized treatment model.

The organization hides the contribution. The uniform frontier theorem, which implies the other three main results, is stated last. The shrinking-overlap proof is derived from it anyway. The main text has no proof sketch, and roughly 80% of the paper is an unstructured appendix that proves the same facts several times: the two-point floor three times, the parametric KL bound twice, the variance assembly twice, the score-mean peeling three times. Fix: state the uniform theorem first and present the fixed-C, C=1 and shrinking-overlap results as corollaries. Add a one-page main-text sketch of the bias–variance balance and of the signed-depth mechanism α^{2Q}L^{-Q}. Merge the duplicated lemmas and inline proof steps.
